chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, with his chain, that he ascribed it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

that it was said to him: (What is the ruling of) A man who drinks in one breath? He said: There is no harm. I said: There are those before us who say that this is (like) the drinking of thirsty cattle? Then he said: The (like of the) drinking of thirsty cattle is only that which the Name of Allah has not been mentioned upon.

key_terms.شَرَبُ الْهِيمِ: The drinking of thirsty cattle; a metaphor for drinking greedily or without mentioning God's name

ai.seo_question: Is it disliked to drink water in one breath according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying that drinking in one breath is permissible, refuting the notion that it constitutes 'sharab al-haym' (the greedy, cattle-like drinking). The Imam specifies that this improper mode of consumption is defined by the absence of mentioning Allah’s Name, thereby linking the physical act to spiritual mindfulness and the Sunnah of reciting *Bismillah* during sustenance.
